# The Kenyan clinical research unit bringing precision cancer medicine to East Africa

  * 15 May 2024
  * Diana Mwango

Clinical cancer trials are being run in East Africa for the first time. Diana Mwango asks triallists, clinicians and global cancer leaders what that could mean for improving access to quality diagnostics and care in the region.

Four years ago, clinical trials were little discussed in oncology circles in Kenya. In common with the rest of East  Africa, there was no clinical research unit to study treatments for non-communicable diseases such as cancer.

No cancer patient living in Kenya had ever been offered experimental therapies as part of a trial in their home country. Now, for the first time, hundreds are being enrolled in two centres in Kenya; information about recruiting trials in breast, lung and oesophagus cancer clinical trials is appearing on social media platforms, and specialists are hosting medical webinars to promote awareness.

## Como é feito o diagnóstico de cancro em animais? #

Dependendo da localização do tumor, este pode ser externo, ou seja, visível ou palpável (como os tumores na pele, na cavidade oral, no olho ou na musculatura), ou interno, sendo diagnosticado através de exames de imagem, como ecografias ou radiografias, que permitem detetar massas em localizações internas. Após a sua identificação, é realizada uma confirmação através de uma colheita de amostra, seja por citologia ou biópsia.

  * Osteossarcoma, cancro nos ossos   
  * Hemangiossarcoma, cancro dos vasos sanguíneos   
  * Melanoma oral   
  * Carcinoma do saco anal   
  * Carcinoma da tiroide, cancro da tiroide   
  * Sarcoma de tecidos moles, cancro nas articulações   
  * Cancro da mama em cadelas   
  * Tumores da cavidade nasal   
  * Carcinoma urotelial, cancro na bexiga 

### Cancros mais comuns em gatos

Nos gatos, os tipos de cancro mais comuns são:

  * Carcinoma de células escamosas na face ou cavidade oral   
  * Carcinomas pulmonares   
  * Carcinomas mamários, tumor de mama em gatos   
  * Cancros intestinais 

## Terapia e tratamento do cancro em animais #

As principais modalidades terapêuticas para tratar o cancro são a cirurgia, a radioterapia e a quimioterapia. Na AniCura tratamos muitos casos de cancro por ano com estas técnicas e outras inovações terapêuticas, como a electro quimioterapia, um novo tratamento oncológico que combina a quimioterapia com a aplicação de impulsos elétricos sobre tumores cutâneos, subcutâneos ou da cavidade oral. Os tumores mais tratados com electro quimioterapia são os carcinomas de células escamosas no nariz dos gatos, causados pela radiação solar. 

## Quais são os sinais que podem indicar que um animal tem cancro? #

Para uma deteção precoce do cancro, deve levar regularmente o seu animal ao veterinário. Além disso, observe o seu cão ou gato no dia a dia e consulte a sua equipa veterinária de confiança se notar sinais como: mudanças de comportamento, alteração da condição corporal ou perda de vitalidade; beber ou urinar mais do que o normal podem indicar dor ou desconforto crónico, que pode ser atribuído a um cancro.

# Oncologia veterinária na prática: diagnóstico e tratamento dos principais tumores em cães e gatos

## Aprenda a identificar, diagnosticar e tratar os tumores mais comuns na rotina clínica, com foco nos protocolos quimioterápicos e nas decisões cirúrgicas fundamentais para o sucesso terapêutico.

A prática oncológica na medicina veterinária exige conhecimento técnico, bom senso clínico e responsabilidade ética. A abordagem de neoplasias em cães e gatos vai além da identificação do tumor. É preciso saber como coletar amostras corretamente, escolher a melhor técnica diagnóstica (citologia ou histopatologia), avaliar a viabilidade cirúrgica, indicar o protocolo quimioterápico adequado e, sobretudo, dialogar com o tutor sobre prognóstico e qualidade de vida.
Nesta matéria, você vai entender o raciocínio clínico por trás da condução de casos oncológicos com base em seis tumores de alta incidência:

1. Carcinoma de células escamosas (CEC ou SEC)
Tumor maligno, localmente destrutivo, comum em cães e gatos brancos expostos à radiação ultravioleta crônica. Acomete focinho, pálpebras, plano nasal, orelhas e abdome ventral.

Diagnóstico:
Preferencialmente por citologia (pAAF, imprint ou swab), evitando manipulação excessiva em lesões ulceradas.

Tratamento:

  * Cirurgia com margens amplas, sempre que possível.

## Global registry

The World Health Organization's International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) acts as a voluntary coordinating body for many international registries, including many of those listed below.

## National and regional registries

### Africa

The Pan-African clinical trials registry (PACTR) is available at pactr.org. It is funded by the European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership (EDCTP) and operates out of the South African Cochrane Centre (Cochrane Collaboration) based at the South African Medical Research Council. PACTR contributes data to the WHO's ICTRP.

### Australia and New Zealand

Australia and New Zealand share the ANZCTR registry located at: anzctr.org.au. Registering trials with the ANZCTR is voluntary. It is publicly owned and managed by a non-profit organization and is funded by an enabling grant from Australia's National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC).
Its search portal is hosted by the Japanese National Institute of Public Health. While the search portal is only available in Japanese, the three registries' sites are also available in English:
* University Hospital Medical Information Network (UMIN CTR)
* Japan Pharmaceutical Information Center - Clinical Trials Information (JapicCTI)
* Japan Medical Association - Center for Clinical Trials (JMACCT CTR)

- WHO - Japan Primary Registries Network (JPRN).

### Netherlands

The Netherlands registry participates with WHO and its website is trialregister.nl. Clinical trial data are available in English.

### South Africa

South Africa's Department of Health announced in November 2005, that clinical trials conducted in the country must be submitted to the South African National Clinical Trials Register located at: sanctr.gov. Clinical trial guidelines for South Africa are available at the Department of Health's official site.

## Durée des études

### Phase de recherche pré-clinique

Avant de lancer un essai clinique de médicament, environ médicaments potentiels ont été testés en laboratoire sur des cellules et des animaux. Les nouvelles molécules potentiellement intéressantes en termes pharmacologiques doivent d'abord être découvertes (l'intelligence artificielle peut grandement accélérer cette phase), purifiées, caractérisées et testées en laboratoire (sur des cellules et des animaux) avant de passer aux essais cliniques. Pour un médicament contre le cancer, en moyenne six ans sont nécessaires pour cette phase préparatoire.

Le premier obstacle à la réalisation des études est souvent le manque de participants adéquats et volontaires généralement bénévoles qui savent qu'ils recevront peut-être un placebo ou au moins un médicament dont l'efficacité n'est pas encore prouvée. Tous les essais de médicaments et de nombreux essais de dispositifs ciblent un sous-ensemble particulier de la population, et certains essais cliniques nécessitent des patients présentant des spécificités génétiques ou des combinaisons inhabituelles de caractéristiques de la maladie.

No cure for cancer in canines exist.

Some dog owners opt for no treatment of the cancer at all, in which case palliative care, including pain relief, may be offered. Regardless of how treatment proceeds following a diagnosis, the quality of life of the pet is an important consideration. In cases where the cancer is not curable, there are still many things which can be done to alleviate the dog's pain. Good nutrition and care from the dog's owner can greatly enhance quality of life.

- Lisa Y. Pang, David J. Argyle. Veterinary oncology: Biology, big data and precision medicine. The Veterinary Journal.
- D Regan, A Guth, J Coy, S Dow. Cancer immunotherapy in veterinary medicine: Current options and new developments. The Veterinary Journal.

## Prognosis

According to Blue Cross, pet owners can expect for their pet to live about 12 months with current treatments. If the owner opts for palliative care instead of treatment, the dog will live about 3 months, although if the tumor is partially removed this can be extended. The survival time may be longer in large dogs, and the cure rate is 20%. If a tumor is completely removed, usually the pet will receive small doses of radiation in hopes of preventing recurrence. The survival rates are: 1 year: 59%, 3 year: 40%, 5 year: 13%.

Due to morphological similarities, the differentiation of histologic sections of cutaneous tumors into individual subtypes can be challenging. Recently, deep learning-based approaches have proven their potential for supporting pathologists in this regard. In inter-rater experiments, we show a high consistency of the provided labels, especially for tumor annotations. Clinical trials (CT) are essential for advancing medical research and treatment, yet efficiently recruiting eligible participants -- each of whom must meet complex eligibility criteria -- remains a significant challenge. Traditional recruitment approaches, such as advertisements or electronic health record screening within hospitals, are often time-consuming and geographically constrained. This work addresses the recruitment challenge by leveraging the vast amount of health-related information individuals share on social media platforms. With the emergence of powerful large language models (LLMs) capable of sophisticated text understanding, we pose the central research question: Can LLM-driven tools facilitate CT recruitment by identifying potential participants through their engagement on social media? To investigate this question, we introduce TRIALQA, a novel dataset comprising two social media collections from the subreddits on colon cancer and prostate cancer. Using eligibility criteria from public real-world CTs, experienced annotators are hired to annotate TRIALQA to indicate (1) whether a social media user meets a given eligibility criterion and (2) the user's stated reasons for interest in participating in CT. We benchmark seven widely used LLMs on these two prediction tasks, employing six distinct training and inference strategies. Our extensive experiments reveal that, while LLMs show considerable promise, they still face challenges in performing the complex, multi-hop reasoning needed to accurately assess eligibility criteria.

Automatic identification of clinical trials for which a patient is eligible is complicated by the fact that trial eligibility is stated in natural language. In this study, we focus on seven common exclusion criteria in cancer trials: prior malignancy, human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, psychiatric illness, drug/substance abuse, and autoimmune illness. Our dataset consists of 764 phase III cancer trials with these exclusions annotated at the trial level. In this work we investigate a mathematical model describing tumour growth under a treatment by chemotherapy that incorporates time-delay related to the conversion from resting to hunting cells.
